case_title: State of Punjab v. Balwinder Singh and Ors.
aggravating_circumstances: Five deaths caused due to rash and negligent driving
trial_court_outcome: Convicted and sentenced to two years rigorous imprisonment under s.304-A and six months rigorous imprisonment under s.337 and s.279
high_court_outcome: Reduced sentence to 15 days and enhanced fine to Rs.25,000/- each
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder
neutral_facts: A motor accident occurred when a bus and a truck collided due to rash and negligent driving by their respective drivers. Five persons traveling in the bus died as a result of the collision. The prosecution established that the drivers were at fault and caused the accident through their careless driving. The trial court convicted the drivers under Sections 304A, 337, and 279 of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced them to two years rigorous imprisonment under Section 304A and six months rigorous imprisonment under Sections 337 and 279. The High Court reduced the sentence to the period already undergone and increased the fine. The Supreme Court overturned the High Court's decision, emphasizing the need for deterrence in cases involving motor accidents and imposed a sentence of six months rigorous imprisonment with a fine of Rs. 5,000/- each.
